title: voice-curation-sprint-pocket-archive-2029-10
body:
Context:
Quick pocket-archive from the voice-curation sprint (Oct 2–9, 2029). This doc is deliberately compact — meant for engineering triage, solutions eng pooling, and PS scoping. Not a canonical synthesis (that comes later) — consider it a prioritized scratchpad of signals we heard, rough impact estimates, and 1–2 tactical fixes per cluster that can be shipped in a week or two.

How we collected:
- 8 customer calls (mid-market + enterprise) coordinated by CS AE team; 12 support threads pulled from Vault; telemetry spikes from Console trace logs (see CONFLUENCE-5248).
- Focus: inference reliability edge cases, rollout primitives, and observability gaps tied to per-route cost anomalies.

Top signal clusters (ranked by immediate business risk):
1) Short-lived KV-cache invalidation causing repeated token generation surges
- What customers said: "We saw token counts spike 3x after a canary revert and our bill doubled for a day" (Large fintech).
- Evidence: Trace samples show cache miss cascades when canary and control both touched same model variant; autoscaling delayed small-instance warmup.
- Rough impact: High cost + latency + SLAs at risk.
- Quick fixes: a) Add an opt-in canary isolation flag to prevent KV sharing during rollout; b) Emit per-request cache-hit metric to Console (small telemetry push).

2) Route-level unit economics opacity (token attribution ambiguous across fallbacks)
- What customers said: "We can't tell if the cheaper fallback model did the heavy lifting or the primary model — costing us messy reconciliations." (SaaS search product)
- Evidence: Billing logs map tokens to customer route but not to model-variant when fallback occurred; Console traces show consolidated token counters.
- Rough impact: Medium revenue disputes, procurement friction.
- Quick fixes: a) Add model-variant id to per-token accounting export (CSV); b) Short-term doc alert: how to interpret current logs (send to customers flagged in Jira).

3) Observability blind spots on private deployments (VPC) — missing sidecar-level traces
- What customers said: "We instrument everything but Redwood's sidecar is a black box. Hard to blame network vs runtime." (regulated healthcare customer)
- Evidence: SRE runbooks show repeated handoffs to support with packet captures; low sampling on private traces.
- Rough impact: High time-to-resolution, longer support cycles.
- Quick fixes: a) Offer a downloadable lightweight sidecar debug bundle (tiered access); b) Increase sampling for private traces for 48h when customers file an incident.

4) Developer experience: function/tool-calling ergonomics — ambiguous errors when external tool timeouts occur
- What customers said: "Tool call failed but our app kept retrying because function schema ambiguity wasn't surfaced" (AI-native startup)
- Evidence: Several Repeater bugs and GH issues where SDK doesn't bubble structured error type.
- Rough impact: Medium developer friction, app-level retries.
- Quick fixes: a) Standardize and document structured error envelope for function calls; b) Patch SDKs to expose error-type constant (patch planned in PR #342).

Small-bet ideas (low effort, exploratory):
- Batching advisor: surface a one-click suggestion in Console for routes with high per-token cost and low latency sensitivity.
- Canary watch: small alert template customers can attach to canaries to detect KV thrash early.

Open questions / risks:
- How much of the KV isolation change is runtime vs orchestration? (ask serving-runtime team for a 30m feasibility sync).
- Sidecar debug bundle requires legal review for customer-supplied artifacts — loop in security-compliance.
- Billing attribution change will need product + finance sign-off; may affect invoices already issued.

Next steps (owners + dates):
- Priya: Draft canary isolation proposal & API sketch (deadline: 2029-10-16).
- Ethan: Console telemetry ticket + CSV export spec (JIRA-CS-1987) (deadline: 2029-10-14).
- Lina: Coordinate private-deploy debug bundle feasibility with eng-private (meeting scheduled 2029-10-12).
- Marcus: Lead SDK error-envelope patch PR and coordinate release notes (target: 2029-10-18).

Immediate ask to triage meeting (Oct 12):
- Serving-runtime: 15m on KV isolation feasibility + impact on latency SLOs.
- Console: 10m on adding model-variant id to exports and per-request cache metrics.
- Product: 10m to evaluate billing change risk and communication plan.

Notes to self / scratchpile:
- Customer A suggested a "shadow billing" CSV — we can prototype for a single account to validate reconciliation flows.
- Link helpful thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CS/threads/ck3f2-trace-sample (internal).

Appendix: raw quotes (redacted)
- "Our morning spike was clearly tied to that canary; we needed a fast switch-off that didn't flush caches across variants."
- "If we can't tell which model charged us, finance refuses to accept month-end charges."
- "We would sign up for a debug bundle even at premium pricing if it reduced our MTTR."

If you want additional structure (full PRD or a customer-facing note), tell me which cluster to expand first. For now this is a sprint pocket archive — short, actionable, and intended to push a few low-risk fixes into backlog grooming.
